Michael —

Thanks for sending the template. Please find our annotated response attached (Sentinel_RFI_answers_v1.pdf) along with a redacted network segmentation snapshot. Quick summary of key points:

- Operator access: We support customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption keys and provide optional operator accounts that can be scoped to jump-hosts and bastion flows.
- Patching/Upgrades: Offline/air-gapped patch bundles are available; our upgrade runner supports staged canary and rollback.
- Backups: Backups are encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys; restore requires both operator approval and a customer-side authorization token.
- Artifacts: We supply signed SBOMs and nightly build signatures; supply chain provenance is included in the runbook attachment.

Attachments included: Sentinel_RFI_answers_v1.pdf (detailed answers), network-segmentation-snapshot.png (redacted), runbook-operator-handoff.docx (operator checklist and handoff).

Hi Laura — thank you for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. A few follow-ups from our engineering & compliance reviewers:

1) Operator key rotation: You mention customer-managed KMS/HSM. Can you describe the operator recovery flow if a KMS key is accidentally deleted? Who holds escrow keys, if any?
2) Offline upgrade workflow: We need explicit steps for an air-gapped upgrade that involves a midstream database schema change. Does your upgrade runner support pre-apply dry-run validation and reversible DB migrations?
3) Evidence of signed artifacts: we see SBOMs — are signatures timestamped and verifiable against a public key?
4) Audit log continuity: when nodes are offline for maintenance, how do you preserve chronological audit trails and ensure immutability upon re-join?

Also, can you confirm the retention period options for operator activity logs and whether logs can be streamed to our Splunk instance over a private peering?

If you can respond in-line in the PDF and include a short runbook excerpt showing an air-gapped upgrade sequence, that will move us forward.

Thanks — looking to lock the review this week.
Michael

Michael —

Appreciate the detailed questions. Below are concise answers and an excerpted upgrade/rollback matrix copied from the runbook we attached. I'll paste the relevant excerpt here and update the PDF with in-line clarifications: 

- KMS/HSM recovery: We do not hold escrow keys by default. For customers who request key escrow, we offer an optional multi-party escrow service (customer ops + Redwood custodial key share) under an executed Addendum. If a customer-managed KMS key is deleted, recovery depends on the KMS vendor (e.g., AWS KMS key recovery window). Our recommended pattern is export encrypted backups prior to rotation and store recovery materials in your HSM-backed vault.

- Offline upgrade (air-gapped) support: Yes — our upgrade runner provides a three-stage process: 
  1) PRE-VALIDATE: local dry-run using production dump and sandbox schema checks;
  2) APPLY: staged node-by-node update with pre-flight health checks; schema migrations are applied with reversible migration scripts where possible;
  3) POST-VERIFY: automated replay of a validation workload and sanity checks.
  If a DB migration is required that is not reversible, we require a pre-signed rollback snapshot of DB state as part of the canary. This is documented in section 3.2 of runbook-operator-handoff.docx.

- Signed artifacts: All release binaries and SBOMs are signed with an internal signing key and timestamped via our timestamp authority (TSA). We publish the signing public key fingerprint and flow in the runbook; signatures are verifiable offline.

- Audit log continuity: Nodes buffer audit events locally in an append-only encrypted ledger. When connectivity is restored, the node performs a signed append operation to a centralized immutable log service. The ledger includes sequence numbers and hash chaining to prevent reordering. We support forwarders to Splunk over private peering (TLS mutual auth).

- Log retention: Operator activity logs: configurable (90/365/custom days) and can be exported to customer SIEM. We recommend a 365-day immutable window for regulated customers.

I'll update the PDF with the in-line Q&A and paste the runbook excerpt under section "Air-gapped upgrade sequence"; attaching revised PDF by EOD.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com

[Quoted excerpt]
Air-gapped upgrade sequence (excerpt):
1) Transfer upgrade bundle to secure media and verify bundle signature via provided public key;
2) Run PRE-VALIDATE against a snapshot; fail-fast if dry-run mismatches > 0.5% of validation tokens;
3) Quiesce workers, snapshot DB, apply migration step with temporary dual-write if needed;
4) Canary 10% of nodes, run verification scripts for 12 hours;
5) If verification passes, progressively roll to remaining nodes; otherwise trigger automated rollback using snapshot.
